title: Two new games you can play basically forever
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Civilization VII
recommendations.blurb: It’s still technically only in early access, but by most accounts, this game lives up to the series’ truly epic, practically unparalleled depth and history. I’ve always avoided these games for fear they’d take over my life — but maybe it’s time.

recommendations.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
recommendations.blurb: Big week for outrageously huge, deliberate, thousands-of-hours games! Warhorse’s new epic seems to be a now-rare, kind of slow, truly open world — which I suspect might be the exact kind of escape people need right now. You know, for Reasons.

recommendations.name: Avoiding Outrage Fatigue while Staying Informed
recommendations.blurb: “ Avoiding Outrage Fatigue while Staying Informed.” A really good Scientific American podcast about a topic that feels, uh, very relevant right now. It’s important to understand what’s happening! But we all need some help to manage it all.

recommendations.name: ChatGPT deep research
recommendations.blurb: The new thing in LLMs is models that can take their time, work through a problem, and come to much better and more useful answers. I’ve only played with deep research a little, but it’s impressive — and even experts are saying it gets most things right.

recommendations.name: Tapestry
recommendations.blurb: I’m kinda done with algorithms, and I think timeline apps like this one, and Reeder, and Feeeed, are going to be a big deal. Put your favorite blogs, creators, podcasts, Bluesky follows, and everything else in one place — Apple devices only, alas — and consume it all at your speed.

recommendations.name: Tana
recommendations.blurb: Tana’s been in beta for a while and has developed into one of the most powerful and power user-friendly productivity apps out there. It’s like an even nerdier Notion — and there’s a lot about it I really like.

recommendations.name: The Z-Suite
recommendations.blurb: Tubi Originals! Are apparently a thing! I’m sort of shocked how fun I found the pilot about a bunch of rowdy youths who take charge at an ad agency. Definitely one to watch after the Super Bowl ( also on Tubi! ) ends this weekend.

recommendations.name: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
recommendations.blurb: “ Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT.” Maybe the best “how does AI actually work” primer I’ve ever seen. It is long — three and a half hours! — but it is both really understandable and really deep, which is hard to pull off. Watch it, and take notes.

recommendations.name: Instapaper 9.1
recommendations.blurb: Instapaper is the OG read-later app and continues to get better. The newest update does a particularly nice job of managing paywalls and logins, which makes the whole process of saving stuff feel much more seamless. (So far, it’s only for iOS, but I assume it’s coming to Android soon.)

recommendations.name: Bluescreen for Bluesky
recommendations.blurb: A nifty iOS app that re-skins Bluesky as a TikTok-like video player and actually works really well. The Bluesky videos are not as good as the TikTok videos, but it’s a really cool concept.

recommendations.name: Cassandra
recommendations.blurb: More high-tech thrillers! This one, on Netflix, is about a smart home assistant gone batty. It’s both extremely creepy and also filled with tech I wish existed in my own house. Just less… murder-y?

recommendations.name: iPhone
recommendations.blurb: The phone: An iPhone — I only buy them used because they are so much cheaper that way!

recommendations.name: Feedly
recommendations.blurb: Of note: I use Feedly for keeping up with RSS feeds and news.

recommendations.blurb: I keep Bluesky on the homescreen as it’s now my main social network, and of course, I keep Signal handy since that’s the main way I communicate every day.

recommendations.name: Fallout: New Vegas
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been replaying Fallout: New Vegas.

recommendations.name: Bleep
recommendations.blurb: Using Bleep. It’s like Google Keep got in a fight with MyMind and agreed to be friends.

recommendations.name: Firewalla
recommendations.blurb: Firewalla. They are a router / firewall company that truly makes an appliance that can be plug-and-play, with a shell available for power users to do more things. They recently also released access points that are also super simple to set up.

recommendations.name: GameTrack
recommendations.blurb: I am looking for a good app to track the games I am playing (or plan to) across various platforms. So far, GameTrack is my favorite, but Game Tracker seems like a good and cheaper entry. (Yes, they have basically the same name but are different apps, not confusing at all.)

recommendations.name: T3 Chat
recommendations.blurb: Using the T3 Chat client instead of the ChatGPT website or Anthropic’s crappy desktop app — turns out just making the webpage fast is an insane improvement to the experience.

recommendations.name: ElevenReader
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been using the ElevenReader app by ElevenLabs to create podcasts from some of those TL;DR articles. It boils them down into a shorter — obviously cruder — form so I can listen to a few while walking the dog.

recommendations.name: Superlist
recommendations.blurb: Trying Superlist again, love the thoughtful and beautiful design and the recent updates. Love that I can log on via web and quickly glance on my iPhone. Love the recent update.

recommendations.name: Moccamaster
recommendations.blurb: Moccamaster for coffee brewing. I’ve been switching back and forth from a pour-over to the Moccamaster the last while. I happened to be drinking a fresh pot when I read your post.

recommendations.name: Androids: The Team that Built the Android Operating System
recommendations.blurb: Finally got around to reading Androids: The Team that Built the Android Operating System. An amazing book to understand how Android came to be, and that made me dig out my old OS college notes. Now I’m reading too much about OSes of the ’90s / 2000s.

recommendations.name: Letterboxd
recommendations.blurb: There’s a group on Letterboxd that runs a monthly movie Scavenger Hunt, with a new host each month, that creates prompts for each day. Like: ‘watch a film from a country you want to visit.’ It really helps expand your movie horizon.

recommendations.name: Sonos Beam (second-gen)
recommendations.blurb: I bought a Sonos Beam (second-gen), and it is such a huge upgrade over my TV’s speakers. I am kicking myself for not doing it years ago.

recommendations.name: WikiTok
recommendations.blurb: WikiTok is just a TikTok feed of Wikipedia pages, and hoo boy is it fun to play with.

recommendations.name: ReddTok
recommendations.blurb: ReddTok flips infinitely through Reddit posts and is way more engaging than the Reddit homepage.
